test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Manju sold a scooty with a tagged price of ₹1,25,000 . After applying a trade concession, the final transaction value became ₹70,000 . Calculate the percentage discount given on the marked price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Tagged Price (MP) to Transaction Value (SP) = 1,25,000 : 70,000 = 125 : 70 = 25 : 14.

Discount units = 25 − 14 = 11 units.

Discount % = (Discount units ÷ MP units) × 100 = (11 ÷ 25) × 100.

Discount % = 11 × 4 = 44%.

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Tagged Price (Marked Price) = ₹1,25,000

Final Transaction Value (Selling Price) = ₹70,000

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = [ (Marked Price − Selling Price) ÷ Marked Price ] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77fe5f23a6bfcbc52d6a4c12422ed93993356a57344cdcac19b810600348eb65.png] 

⇒ Discount = ₹1,25,000 − ₹70,000

⇒ Discount = ₹55,000

⇒ Discount % = (55,000 ÷ 1,25,000) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (55 ÷ 125) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (11 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 11 × 4 = 44%

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to reach the marked price: Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Selling Price Formula

SP can be calculated directly using MP and discount: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.
